clue.text: Husky, say, might achieve this rate of work

definitions.text: Husky, say, might achieve this rate of work

parts.words: Husky, say, might achieve this rate of work
parts.note: a husky is a sledge dog doing the hauling job a horse would do, so its output is measured in the engineer's unit of work rate named after that animal

explanation.surface: A question of how much work a sled dog can do.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a husky pulls like a horse, so its effort is fittingly rated in the unit named after horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit is a standard measure of the rate at which an engine or animal does mechanical work.

clue.text: Baronet falls in river? How stupid

indicators.note: the baronet drops into the river, so his abbreviation goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (several in fact), a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman tumbles into a river and someone exclaims at his foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' just sets up the exclamation and is a link word; the definition is 'stupid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone slow to understand, dull-witted.

clue.text: One of a Mexican's overheads, it may be felt

definitions.text: One of a Mexican's overheads, it may be felt

parts.words: One of a Mexican's overheads, it may be felt
parts.note: overheads sounds like business costs but means things worn on the head, and felt is the hat-making fabric rather than the past tense of feel

explanation.surface: A remark about a Mexican firm's running costs and how keenly they are felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' suggests business expenses and 'felt' suggests feeling; really they are hats and the material they are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: This wide-brimmed hat is typical Mexican headgear, often made of felt or straw.

clue.text: Page about choice of words used in prophecy

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
diction is a speaker's or writer's choice of words

explanation.surface: A page discussing the wording used in a prophetic text.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction is a forecast of what will happen, as a prophecy is.

clue.text: The president's loss of weight is standing up to examination

indicators.note: the president loses the weight, so those letters are removed from his name

parts.note: George Washington was the first US president
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A president has lost weight and is coping well with a medical check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'that won't wash' means an excuse fails scrutiny, so something washing does stand up to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash, informally, is to be convincing or hold good when tested, as an argument or excuse.

clue.text: Smuggled diamonds to get foreign currency

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran is smuggled
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Diamond smuggling as a way of getting hold of foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the currency unit of South Africa, which to a British setter is foreign money.

clue.text: Formal interview sought by players

definitions.meaning: a formal meeting granted by a monarch or the Pope
actors and musicians want people watching and listening

explanation.surface: Performers seeking a formal interview.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal hearing with a dignitary and the crowd of spectators performers hope to draw.

clue.text: It's found, aptly enough, in the musician's kitchen

definitions.text: It's found, aptly enough, in the musician's kitchen

parts.words: It's found, aptly enough, in the musician's kitchen
parts.note: a kitchen holds a pot for boiling water, and a musician's version would be the orchestral drum named after that pot

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what you would find in a musician's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument's name begins with a kitchen utensil, which is why it is apt in a musician's kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This orchestral drum, also called a timpano, has a bowl shaped like a large pot.

clue.text: Decoy a couple of students into a river

indicators.note: the students go into a river, so their letters sit inside the letters for a river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular
L is a learner or student, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: Luring two students into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' (of 'a couple') is a link word; the second 'a' joins the river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure means to entice or tempt, as a decoy draws its prey.

clue.text: Speaks imperfectly, but somehow masters opening of "Macbeth"

indicators.note: somehow says the letters end up in some new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor stumbles over the start of Macbeth yet somehow masters it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges MASTERS together with M, the first letter of 'Macbeth'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stammer is to speak with halting repetitions, a form of faulty speech.

clue.text: Fellow involved in robbery is out for pleasure

indicators.note: the fellow is caught up in the robbery, so his letters go inside the robbery word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man involved in a robbery is out for a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' suggests HE or MAN, but here it is a college don.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for enjoyment, always seeking gratification.

clue.text: Surrender the church keys

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
D and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: Handing over the keys of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or yield something, such as territory.

clue.text: Accountant tempted a Scotsman — an old one

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to lead someone on is to tempt or entice them
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An accountant leads astray an elderly Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an old one' refers back to 'a Scotsman': the answer is an ancient Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia was the Roman name for northern Britain, so its people were the ancient Scots.

clue.text: Learn the technique that can make us all Cowards?

definitions.text: that can make us all Cowards?

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to learn or study
science here is skill or technique, as in the science of boxing

explanation.surface: Learning the method that turns everyone into a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'Thus conscience does make cowards of us all'; the capital C on Cowards is a nod to Noel Coward too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's soliloquy blames the inner moral sense for making people too timid to act.

clue.text: Novel recalled in a fairy-tale

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A novel that recalls a fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal on RECALLED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This rags-to-riches story of a girl with a glass slipper is a famous fairy tale.

clue.text: The trick in amateur circles is using few words

indicators.note: the amateur surrounds the trick, so its letters circle the other word

parts.note: laic means lay, not professional or clerical
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: An amateur conjurer's trick is to say very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse and brief, after the clipped style of the Spartans.

clue.text: Splendid, when he fights for the cause

definitions.meaning: an old informal word for excellent

definitions.text: when he fights for the cause
definitions.meaning: a person who defends or argues for a cause

explanation.surface: Praise for a man who fights for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both dated slang for first-rate and a noun for a defender of a cause.

clue.text: The aardvark is unable to endure being beheaded

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter of the phrase

parts.note: if you cannot endure something you can't bear it

explanation.surface: An aardvark that cannot stand the thought of execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beheaded' takes the C off CANTBEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal that eats ants, hence its other name.

clue.text: Roared out that Acton, say, was in debt

parts.note: Acton Bell was the pen name of Anne Brontë, so Acton is an example of a Bell
owed means was in debt

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that Acton was in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton reads as the London district; it is Anne Brontë's pseudonym Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellowed means shouted loudly, like a bull's roar.

clue.text: Useful hint from a Pickwickian about 6

indicators.note: the Pickwickian goes about the other letter, so it sits inside his name

parts.note: Nathaniel Winkle is a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers
6 refers to the answer at 6 down, the South African currency, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A tip from a Dickens character about some cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6' is a cross-reference to 6 down, whose abbreviation is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle, informally, is a clever tip or trick worth knowing.

clue.text: Its huge trunk an impediment to an actor?

definitions.text: Its huge trunk an impediment to an actor?

parts.words: Its huge trunk an impediment to an actor?
parts.note: the tree's name splits into a phrase meaning something that holds back a performer, with a trunk being both its stem and a costume chest

explanation.surface: A performer hampered by an enormous costume trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's first part as 'drag on', a hindrance, hinting at a theatre trunk that weighs an actor down; really it is a tree with a massive trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This Canary Islands tree, a dracaena, is known for its thick trunk and red resin.

clue.text: Appear indistinctly as part of an oar

definitions.meaning: to come into view vaguely and threateningly
the shaft of an oar, between blade and handle

explanation.surface: Something vaguely visible as part of an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for emerging dimly and a rowing term for the inboard shaft of an oar.

clue.text: Brutus, for one, raised thanks when surrounded by gold

indicators.note: the thanks is enclosed by gold, so its letters sit between gold letters

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Brutus raises his thanks while surrounded by gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TA into AT; the setter lets gold, OR, sit on both sides of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus makes a famous public speech in Julius Caesar, so he is an example of a speechmaker.

clue.text: Coin used in card game

definitions.meaning: a trick-taking game, also called nap

explanation.surface: A coin used in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor's name is both an old French gold coin and a card game like whist.

clue.text: Poems some old Scandinavians composed daily

indicators.note: some of the words are used, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Ancient Scandinavians writing poems every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Scandinavians' describes the poems' authors and supplies no letters; the run sits across 'composed daily'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are old Icelandic collections of Norse myth and verse.

clue.text: Amount of power required to walk it, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: How much energy it takes to go for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a thousand watts, a unit of electrical power.

clue.text: A body of examiners possibly at sea

parts.note: a board is a panel of examiners or interviewers

explanation.surface: An examining panel that may be all at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' suggests confusion, but means on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship, so a passenger aboard is out on the water.

clue.text: Nevski's plant?

parts.note: Nevski was the Russian prince Alexander, and the plant's name sounds like it belongs to people with his first name

explanation.surface: Asking what plant belongs to the Russian hero Nevski.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name looks like the plural of the prince's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a yellow-flowered umbellifer once grown as a pot herb.
